findings.title: get_monitor_environment_context computes a modified config but returns the unmodified one
findings.body: The function builds a local `config` copy, replaces `config['schedule_type']` with its human-readable display value, and then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the original, unmodified dict) in the `"config"` key of the context. The computed `config` variable is never used. Consequence: the monitor context sent with the occurrence event contains the raw schedule_type value (e.g. an enum/int) instead of the display string, so any consumer of this context (issue display, grouping, alerting) sees the wrong value. This is a behavior regression relative to the apparent intent (and likely relative to the pre-refactor code this was moved from, if it differed).

findings.title: get_failure_reason can raise KeyError when a single failed check-in has a status outside the known maps
findings.body: The Counter is filtered to statuses present in HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP, so `status_counts` can be empty (e.g. a check-in with status OK or an unknown status value). If exactly one check-in is passed but its status is not in the map, `sum(status_counts.values()) == 1` is False (it is 0), so execution falls through to `get_text_list([])` and returns the plural template with an empty list — producing a nonsense message like " check-ins detected". Additionally, if `status_counts` has exactly one entry the code indexes `SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP[list(status_counts.keys())[0]]`, which is safe only because the Counter is pre-filtered to the same keys; any future divergence between the two maps would raise KeyError. findings.title: Occurrences are created for check-ins in arbitrary DB order, not chronological order
findings.body: The loop fetches `MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=[...])` with no `order_by`, so the queryset returns rows in unspecified (typically primary-key/insertion) order. `create_incident_occurrence` is then called once per check-in, each producing an occurrence whose `received`/`timestamp` and evidence reflect that specific check-in. Because `previous_checkins` was explicitly reversed to be oldest-first (line 48 comment: 'reverse the list after slicing in order to start with oldest check-in'), the intent is clearly to process them chronologically, but the re-fetch discards that ordering. Consequence: occurrence `timestamp`/`received` values and any per-checkin evidence (e.g. trace_id from `failed_checkin.trace_id`) are attached to check-ins in a non-deterministic order, which can produce out-of-order occurrences in the issue stream and non-deterministic `received` timestamps for the same incident. An explicit `.order_by('date_added')` (or iterating `previous_checkins` and fetching each) is needed to preserve the intended ordering.

findings.title: Variable `incident` may be referenced before assignment when status transitions to ERROR
findings.body: In the `MonitorStatus.OK/ACTIVE` branch, `incident` is declared with the annotation `incident: MonitorIncident | None` on line 61 and then assigned via `get_or_create` on line 62. In the `elif monitor_env.status == MonitorStatus.ERROR` branch it is assigned from `monitor_env.active_incident`. The `else` branch returns early, so all paths that reach line 92 have assigned `incident`. However, the annotation-only declaration on line 61 is a bare annotation with no value; if `get_or_create` were ever skipped or the code restructured, line 92's `and incident` would raise UnboundLocalError rather than evaluating to a safe default. This is a latent fragility introduced by the move (the annotation line is new in this module), not an active bug today, but initializing `incident = None` alongside the annotation would make the contract explicit and match the declared type.

Sentry's isort/ruff configuration orders `sentry.monitors.logic` after `sentry.monitors.models` alphabetically ('logic' > 'models' is false, but the project's known-first-party ordering and typical isort force_sort_within_sections place `models` before `logic` since 'l' < 'm'). This will likely be flagged by the project's lint/CI (ruff I001) and should be reordered to keep CI green.
